# checkgx

> Inspect a check registry for checks that cannot fail. Reports problems with stable codes and exit codes, and writes an annotated storyboard.

checkgx is one of the `gxkit` agent-native review tools. Declare the checks an
artifact writes, the ones its runner actually evaluates, and the keys that sit
beside them as metadata; `checkgx inspect` names duplicates, checks nothing reads,
names read but never declared, and checks that landed among the metadata.

It reads the registry, not the predicates: a check that cannot fail inside its
body is invisible here, which is why the standing `not-a-proof-of-failure`
warning exists rather than silence.

## Install

```sh
uvx --from "git+https://github.com/nekomario28/gxkit#subdirectory=packages/checkgx" checkgx inspect checks.py
# local:  uvx --from ../../packages/checkgx checkgx inspect checks.py
```

## Use

A registry file defines `registry` (a `Registry`) or module-level `CHECKS` /
`REGISTRY`:

```python
import checkgx as c

registry = c.Registry(
    checks=["a_probe_passes", "strings_match", "strings_match"],  # as written, duplicates kept
    evaluated=["a_probe_passes", "strings_match"],  # what the runner reads
    metadata=["status", "note"],  # never evaluated
)
```

## Checks

error: `duplicate-check`, `check-in-metadata`, `check-never-evaluated`,
  `evaluated-but-undeclared`, `no-checks`.
warn: `not-a-proof-of-failure`.

Full documentation is in `README.md`.
